prompt:
A modern open-plan office floor seen from the east end: three bands of back-to-back bench desks with desk-mounted privacy screens and task chairs, a floor-to-ceiling glazed facade on the right, a tall slatted storage volume on the left, structural columns along the facade.

Interior architectural photography, 24 mm tilt-shift lens, two-point perspective with perfectly straight vertical lines, soft overcast daylight from the floor-to-ceiling glazing, realistic material response, natural dynamic range, crisp detail, no text, no signage, no CG or 3D-render look.

FIXED DESIGN DECISIONS — these override anything above, follow every line exactly:
· the original building soffit left exposed and painted dark grey, with visible ducts, cable trays and sprinkler pipework
· bare glazing with no blinds
· continuous recessed linear LED lines running along the desk bands
· dark blue-grey carpet tiles
· minimalist furniture: white and light grey, flush surfaces, concealed fixings, nothing cluttered
· fabric acoustic desk screens about 1.2 m high with slim aluminium trim
· a warm timber and neutral palette
· no people in the frame

The reference image is an UNTEXTURED WHITE MASSING MODEL — every surface is placeholder grey, there is no material, colour or lighting information in it whatsoever. Take ONLY the geometry, camera and object positions from it. Invent all materials, colours, textures and lighting yourself, strictly following the fixed design decisions below.

The reference image is a SIMPLIFIED MASSING MODEL, not a finished render. Every plain block in it is a placeholder standing for a real object at that exact position, size and orientation. Replace each placeholder with properly detailed real-world furniture and fittings: ergonomic mesh-back task chairs with contoured seats, adjustable armrests, gas lift and five-star castor bases; bench desk systems with slim square legs, under-desk cable trays and cable grommets; slim-bezel monitors on articulated arms, keyboards and mice; a few believable personal items. Keep unchanged: the camera and framing, the room shape, the number of desks and chairs, the aisle widths, the ceiling height, and the window mullion spacing. The result must read as a photograph of a completed, occupied office — never as a 3D render, never with blocky simplified furniture.
